$comment: The short cuts (cuts.mjs). Each beat is one voice line over shots taken from the full film's no-captions render: { scene, from } is seconds into that scene of timeline.<theme>.json, { key } is just after that compare key was pressed. Shots share the beat's length evenly unless they set `dur`. Lines take {{runMinutes}} and the same pronunciation rules as script.json.

beats.text: Ten redesigns of one site, all running for real. Here's the whole run, in ninety seconds.
I'm Joaquin. I built Variantly so you don't have to choose one direction and hope. Run npx variantly. Next.js, Django, plain HTML: it finds them.
Pick how many, and give each one its own direction, or leave it blank and Impeccable picks. Then the review shows the cost first: ten variants, twenty sessions on your own plan.
In real time, this run took {{runMinutes}} minutes. Here it is, sped up. Each variant gets its own git worktree, so your main branch is never touched.

Then compare, on your real site, not screenshots. Drag for a before and after. Quiet minimalism. Maximalist collage. Cinematic drama. Expressive type. Press I: accessibility and Lighthouse scores against your original. Hate them all? Run it again. Nothing is kept until you press Keep.
Keep one, and a last pass rolls it out to every page. It lands in your working tree, so you review it like any other change. Nothing is committed.
Free and open source. Run npx variantly. It's at variantly.style.
